source.title: The NAS Parallel Benchmarks
source.reference: NASA Ames NAS Technical Report RNR-94-007, March 1994, §3.3.2
source.algorithm_attribution: point symmetric successive over-relaxation on a regular seven-block-diagonal 3-D operator
source.implementation_status: bounded clean-room SSOR core profile; CFD state, forcing, and boundary generation are omitted

contract.profile: Apply a fixed number of point SSOR sweeps to an explicit 3-D regular sparse operator with five unknowns per grid point.
contract.ordering: Grid points are lexicographic with x fastest, then y, then z. Each point stores five consecutive components.
contract.matrix: K has one shared symmetric 5x5 diagonal block D and three scalar-identity lower-neighbor blocks in x, y, z. Each corresponding upper block is the transpose. Missing out-of-domain neighbors contribute zero.
contract.iteration: For each sweep, compute r=b-Kx, solve (D+Y)y=r in forward lexicographic order, solve (D+Z)z=D y in reverse order, set x=x+z with omega=1, then record the explicit Euclidean norm ||b-Kx||.
contract.scope: This bounded coefficient family exercises the five-component seven-block SSOR data flow. Supplied operator coefficients, right-hand side, and starting state replace NASA's PDE-derived coefficients, forcing, boundary-state construction, and full time-step schedule; this is not a canonical NPB-LU CFD run.

input.encoding: [nx, ny, nz, sweeps, D[25] row-major, cx, cy, cz, rhs[5*points], initial_x[5*points]]
input.matrix_domain: D is exactly symmetric, positive on its diagonal, and strictly row-diagonally dominant after including twice the absolute value of each active direction's scalar-identity coupling; this certifies the symmetric global operator K is positive definite

workspace.meaning: Bound for current state, residual, forward solution, backward correction, and block-solver scratch at 32 grid points.
